claims.text: Tungsten carbide synthesized under controlled high-temperature conditions exhibits enhanced catalytic activity for HER and HOR.
Tungsten carbide synthesized under controlled high-temperature conditions exhibits enhanced durability for HER and HOR.
Tungsten carbide has a platinum-like electronic structure.
Tungsten carbide has inherent corrosion resistance.
High-temperature carburization can convert a tungsten precursor into phase-pure tungsten carbide with controlled morphology.
High-temperature phosphidation can convert a tungsten precursor into phase-pure tungsten carbide with controlled morphology.
The platinum-like electronic structure of tungsten carbide facilitates favorable hydrogen adsorption and desorption kinetics.
Favorable hydrogen adsorption and desorption kinetics improve HER and HOR activity.
The robust carbide structure resists corrosion and catalyst degradation during electrochemical cycling.
Tungsten carbide will exhibit lower HER and HOR overpotentials than baseline non-precious-metal catalysts.
Tungsten carbide will exhibit longer operational stability for HER and HOR than baseline non-precious-metal catalysts.
The improvement depends on tungsten carbide synthesis quality.
Extreme acidic conditions or impurities may alter the catalyst surface and reduce the proposed improvement.

contradictions.description: The intervention proposes either phosphidation or carburization as routes to phase-pure tungsten carbide, while the hypothesis and mediator specifically require a carbide lattice. Phosphidation ordinarily denotes formation of a phosphide rather than a carbide, so this branch of the intervention is internally inconsistent with the stated product.
